Sam McPherson walked down Main Street, past the shoe store, the bakery, and the candy store kept by Penny Hughes, toward a group lounging at the front of Geiger's drug store. arxiv-2008-04155.title: On the Oval Shapes of Beach Stones
arxiv-2008-04155.creator: Theodore P. Hill
arxiv-2008-04155.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Theodore P. Hill. This article introduces a new geophysical theory, in the form of a single simple partial integro-differential equation, to explain how frictional abrasion alone of a stone on a planar beach can lead to the oval shapes observed empirically.

arxiv-2211-01394.title: Self-Similar Gravitational Dynamics, Singularities and Criticality in 2D
arxiv-2211-01394.creator: Upamanyu Moitra
arxiv-2211-01394.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Upamanyu Moitra. We initiate a systematic study of continuously self-similar (CSS) gravitational dynamics in two dimensions, motivated by critical phenomena observed in higher dimensional gravitational theories. We consider CSS spacetimes admitting a homothetic Killing vector (HKV) field. For a general two-dimensional gravitational theory coupled to a dilaton field and Maxwell field, we find that the assumption of continuous self-similarity determines the form of the dilaton coupling to the curvature.

arxiv-2504-05193.title: Observation of coherent \Pgf meson photoproduction in ultraperipheral PbPb collisions at \sqrtsNN = 5.36 ​ \TeV \sqrtsNN=5.36\TeV
arxiv-2504-05193.description: Abstract The first observation of coherent \Pgf meson photoproduction off heavy nuclei is presented using ultraperipheral lead-lead collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.36 \TeV . The data were collected by the CMS experiment and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 1.68 \mubinv .

arxiv-2511-17516.title: A Dynamic Take on Window Management
arxiv-2511-17516.creator: Rohit Chouhan
arxiv-2511-17516.description: Abstract On modern computers with graphical user interfaces, application windows are managed by a window manager, a core component of the desktop environment. Mainstream operating systems such as Microsoft Windows and Apple’s macOS employ window managers, where users rely on a mouse or trackpad to manually resize, reposition, and switch between overlapping windows.

pmc-11428747.title: Why Do People Choose a Particular Dog? A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Factors Owners Consider Important When Acquiring a Dog, on a Convenience Sample of Austrian Pet Dog Owners
pmc-11428747.creator: Kata Mária Udvarhelyi-Tóth, Ivaylo B. Iotchev, Eniko Kubinyi, Borbála Turcsán
pmc-11428747.description: Simple SummaryChoosing the right dog that fits well with an owner’s lifestyle is important for the happiness of both the dog and the owner. This study looked into why and how people in Austria choose their dogs by surveying over a thousand dog owners. Unlike past studies, we asked open-ended questions so that the owners could freely share their reasons.

pmc-11714082.creator: Tomoki T Mitani, Kosei Yamaura, Katsuhiko Matsumoto, Rikuhiro Yamada, Etsuo A Susaki, Hiroki R Ueda
pmc-11714082.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn aging societies, neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, are receiving attention. pmc-12581049.title: Exploring the influence of human-animal bonds on suicide characteristics: cross-sectional study of human-animal bond associated suicide in the USA using the National Violent Death Reporting System
pmc-12581049.creator: Andreina Giron, Rebecca John, Alice Martino, Laura F Goodman, Peter Yu, Maryam Gholizadeh, Marizen R Ramirez, John Schomberg
pmc-12581049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe human-animal bond has been proposed as a factor in the psychological well-being of individuals. This study examines the distribution and characteristics of suicide precipitated by pet loss or concerns about their welfare. We hypothesise that decedents of suicide precipitated by the loss or welfare concern for animal companions will have characteristics that are significantly different from the general population of suicide decedents.MethodsWe analysed National Violent Death Reporting System suicide data 2003–2021. We categorised them into animal-bond-associated (ABA) and non-ABA (NABA).

pmc-12679230.title: Insights into mitofusin-2 and endoplasmic reticulum stress regulation in adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells senescence
pmc-12679230.creator: Fang Lin, Ke-Xin Ma, Xiao-Ting Liang
pmc-12679230.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This article comments on the study by Fang, which demonstrates that reduced nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2 (NRF2) activity promotes endoplasmic reticulum stress and senescence in adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells from hypertrophic obese mice, primarily through downregulation of mitofusin-2 (MFN2). Robust methodologies, including knockdown/rescue experiments, chromatin immunoprecipitation quantitative polymerase chain reaction, co-immunoprecipitation, and transplantation assays, substantiate that NRF2 or MFN2 disruption impairs the therapeutic potential of these cells in insulin resistance.

pmc-13064921.title: Impact of idiopathic short stature on children’s well-being: a nationwide study of short Danish children
pmc-13064921.creator: Anders Juul, Agnès Linglart, Michael Højby, Tina Lund Leunbach, Alberto Pietropoli, Kasper Løwe Lundgren, Lasse de Fries Jensen
pmc-13064921.description: ContextIt remains unclear whether idiopathic short stature (ISS), defined as a height below −2.0 SD score (SDS) without an identifiable cause, adversely affects psychosocial well-being.ObjectiveTo assess the psychosocial impact of ISS in children using nationwide registry and survey data.DesignThe nationwide cohort study included children identified between 2012 and 2020 with follow-up questionnaire data up until 2022.SettingSchool-aged children in Denmark.

pmc-13065953.title: Combining federated learning and travelling model boosts performance and opens opportunities for digital health equity
pmc-13065953.creator: Raissa Souza, Emma A. M. Stanley, Erik Y. Ohara, Richard Camicioli, Oury Monchi, Zahinoor Ismail, Matthias Wilms, Nils D. Forkert
pmc-13065953.description: Federated learning (FL) and travelling model (TM) allow privacy-preserving model training across sites without sharing patient-sensitive data. While both approaches have shown success, they face unique challenges related to distribution shifts between sites. To address this, we propose FedTM, a hybrid framework combining the strengths of FL and TM.

pmc-13642888.creator: Jia-Jia Yun, Ya-Lei Li, Jing-Man Qiu, Yu Yang, Dan-Tong Han, Xiao-Han Yang, Chao Lv, Chao Ren
